full_judgment:
2. The facts involved in case, in short, are that the predecessor of respondent Nos. 1 and 59-61 instituted the above Title Suit No. 207 of 1981, which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 391 of 1984, praying for a decree for partition in respect of the suit land described at the schedule ‘Ka’ to the plaint stating, inter-alia, that Nazimuddin Sarder was the owner to the extent of 11 annas 6 gandas share of the total quantum of land measuring 3.73 acres appertaining to S.A. Khatian number 45 under Badarpur Mouza of Gournadi, District-Barisal and he died in the month of Baishakh, 1371 B.S. at the age of 92 years leaving behind two sons namely, Abdul Aziz and Abdul Mazid and five daughters named Ahez Banu Bibi, Kutu Banu, Jamila, Alimjan Bibi and Chuti Banu Ahez Banu Bibi but during the last 10 years before his death Nazimuddin Sarder due to illness became insane and the plaintiff, being an heir, inherited to the extent of 1 anna and 14 gandas measuring .3934 acres of land i.e. the suit land and he has been possessing the same and the rest of the land are being possessed by the successive heirs of Nazimuddin Sarder and other recorded tenants and those heirs have been made defendants in the present suit; that the plaintiff having felt difficulty in ejmali possession, asked the defendants for partition of his share but the defendant No. 1 refused to partition the suit land expressing that he has acquired 2.7934 acres of land out of suit land by the kabala dated the 10th Falgoon, 1364 B.S.; Nazimuddin Sarder became insane long before 1364 B.S. and he used to live with his sons and he did not execute and register the alleged kabala and/or deliver possession of the land as mentioned in the kabala dated the 10th Falgoon, 1364 B.S. in favour of the defendant No. 1 and the alleged kabala is forged one and no consideration passed against the said kabala and it has now been revealed that the defendant No. 1, on the basis of the said forged kabala, has also executed another kabala on the 20th Ashwin, 1375 B.S. in favour of his brother Abdul Aziz wherein no consideration has also passed and the above document is also a paper transaction. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable and is also barred by principle of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel; Nazimuddin Sarder, being the owner of his share to the extent of 11 annas 6 gandas of S.A. Khatian No. 45, sold out the same by a registered kabala dated the 10th Falgoon, 1364 B.S. to the defendant No. 1 and also delivered possession of the same to the defendant No. 1, who out of the above sold out land and has transferred .88 acres of land by kabala dated the 20th Ashwin, 1375 B.S. in favour of his brother Abdul Aziz; the other recorded tenants Gaher Ali and Bhanu Bibi, also transferred their share by the registered kabala dated 04.05.1962 to Rattan Ali Sarder, son of the defendant No. 1 and delivered possession to him; that the kabala dated the 10th Falgoon, 1364 B.S. is not forged one and after the death of said Abdul Aziz, his son sold out his share and handed over possession of the same to Rattan Ali Sarder by two registered Kabalas and even then Rattan Ali Sarder was not made party in the suit.
